numbering: Standard 700-verse canon; Chapter 13 has 34 verses and excludes Arjuna's alternate opening question.
sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Arjuna.
2:   If men forsake the holy ordinance,
3:   Heedless of Shastras, yet keep faith at heart
4:   And worship, what shall be the state of those,
5:   Great Krishna! Sattwan, Rajas, Tamas? Say!
6: 
7:   Krishna.
8:   Threefold the faith is of mankind and springs
9:   From those three qualities,--becoming "true,"
10:   Or "passion-stained," or "dark," as thou shalt hear!
11: 
12:   The faith of each believer, Indian Prince!
13:   Conforms itself to what he truly is.
14:   Where thou shalt see a worshipper, that one
15:   To what he worships lives  assimilate,
16:   [Such as the shrine, so is the votary,]
17:   The "soothfast" souls adore true gods; the souls
18:   Obeying Rajas worship Rakshasas[FN#34]
19:   Or Yakshas; and the men of Darkness pray
20:   To Pretas and to Bhutas.[FN#35] Yea, and those
21:   Who  practise bitter penance, not enjoined
22:   By rightful rule--penance which hath its root
23:   In self-sufficient, proud hypocrisies--
24:   Those men, passion-beset, violent, wild,
25:   Torturing--the witless ones--My elements
26:   Shut in fair company within their flesh,
27:   (Nay, Me myself, present within the flesh!)
28:   Know them to devils devoted, not to Heaven!
29:   For like as foods are threefold for mankind
30:   In nourishing, so is there threefold way
31:   Of worship, abstinence, and almsgiving!
32:   Hear this of Me! there is a food which brings
33:   Force, substance, strength, and health, and joy to live,
34:   Being well-seasoned, cordial, comforting,
35:   The "Soothfast" meat. And there be foods which bring
36:   Aches and unrests, and burning blood, and grief,
37:   Being too biting, heating, salt, and sharp,
38:   And therefore craved by too strong appetite.
39:   And there is foul food--kept from over-night,[FN#36]
40:   Savourless, filthy, which the foul will eat,
41:   A feast of rottenness, meet for the lips
42:   Of such as love the "Darkness."
43: 
44:   Thus with rites;--
45:   A sacrifice not for rewardment made,
46:   Offered in rightful wise, when he who vows
47:   Sayeth, with heart devout, "This I should do!"
48:   Is "Soothfast" rite. But sacrifice for gain,
49:   Offered for good repute, be sure that this,
50:   O Best of Bharatas! is Rajas-rite,
51:   With stamp of "passion." And a sacrifice
52:   Offered against the laws, with no due dole
53:   Of food-giving, with no accompaniment
54:   Of hallowed hymn, nor largesse to the priests,
55:   In faithless celebration, call it vile,
56:   The deed of "Darkness!"--lost!
57: 
58:   Worship of gods
59:   Meriting worship; lowly reverence
60:   Of Twice-borns, Teachers, Elders; Purity,
61:   Rectitude, and the Brahmacharya's vow,
62:   And not to injure any helpless thing,--
63:   These make a true religiousness of Act.
64: 
65:   Words causing no man woe, words ever true,
66:   Gentle and pleasing words, and those ye say
67:   In murmured reading of a Sacred Writ,--
68:   These make the true religiousness of Speech.
69: 
70:   Serenity of soul, benignity,
71:   Sway of the silent Spirit, constant stress
72:   To sanctify the Nature,--these things make
73:   Good rite, and true religiousness of Mind.
74: 
75:   Such threefold faith, in highest piety
76:   Kept, with no hope of gain, by hearts devote,
77:   Is perfect work of Sattwan, true belief.
78: 
79:   Religion shown in act of proud display
80:   To win good entertainment, worship, fame,
81:   Such--say I--is of Rajas, rash and vain.
82: 
83:   Religion followed by a witless will
84:   To torture self, or come at power to hurt
85:   Another,--'tis of Tamas, dark and ill.
86: 
87:   The gift lovingly given, when one shall say
88:   "Now must I gladly give!" when he who takes
89:   Can render nothing back; made in due place,
90:   Due time, and to a meet recipient,
91:   Is gift of Sattwan, fair and profitable.
92: 
93:   The gift selfishly given, where to receive
94:   Is hoped again, or when some end is sought,
95:   Or where the gift is proffered with a grudge,
96:   This is of Rajas, stained with impulse, ill.
97: 
98:   The gift churlishly flung, at evil time,
99:   In wrongful place, to base recipient,
100:   Made in disdain or harsh unkindliness,
101:   Is gift of Tamas, dark; it doth not bless![FN#37]
102: 
103:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER XVII. OF THE  BHAGAVAD-GITA,
104:   Entitled "Sraddhatrayavibhagayog,"
105:   Or "The Book of Religion by the Threefold Kinds of Faith."

paratext.text:
HERE ENDETH CHAPTER XVII. OF THE  BHAGAVAD-GITA,
  Entitled "Sraddhatrayavibhagayog,"
  Or "The Book of Religion by the Threefold Kinds of Faith."

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः।
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥
records.iast:
arjuna uvāca
ye śāstravidhimutsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ
teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  If men forsake the holy ordinance,
  Heedless of Shastras, yet keep faith at heart
  And worship, what shall be the state of those,
  Great Krishna! Sattwan, Rajas, Tamas? Say!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.1 Arjuna said Those who, setting aside the ordinances of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith, what is their condition, O Krishna? Is is Sattva, Rajas or Tamas?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.1 "Arjuna asked: My Lord! Those who do acts of sacrifice, not according to the scriptures but nevertheless with implicit faith, what is their condition? Is it one of Purity, of Passion or of Ignorance?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.1 Arjuna said But, ['But' is used to present a standpoint distinct from the earlier ones understand from 16.23-4.-S.] O Krsna, what is the state [i.e., where do the rites undertaken by them end?] of those who, endued with faith, adore [Adore-perform sacrifices, distribute wealth etc. in honour of gods and others.] by ignoring the injunctions of the scriptures? Is it sattva, rajas or tamas?

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  Threefold the faith is of mankind and springs
  From those three qualities,--becoming "true,"
  Or "passion-stained," or "dark," as thou shalt hear!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.2 The Blessed Lord said Threefold is the faith of the embodied, which is inherent in their nature the Sattvic (pure), the Rajasic (passionate) and the Tamasic (dark). Do thou hear of it.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.2 Lord Shri Krishna replied: Man has an inherent faith in one or another of the Qualities -Purity, Passion and Ignorance. Now listen.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.2 The Blessed Lord said That faith of the embodied beings, born of their own nature, is threefold-born of sattva, rajas and tamas. Hear about it.

records.sanskrit:
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत।
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
records.iast:
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata
śraddhāmayo.ayaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The faith of each believer, Indian Prince!
  Conforms itself to what he truly is.
  Where thou shalt see a worshipper, that one
  To what he worships lives  assimilate,
  [Such as the shrine, so is the votary,]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.3 The faith of each is in accordance with his nature, O Arjuna. The man consists of his faith; as a man's faith is, so is he.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.3 The faith of every man conforms to his nature. By nature he is full of faith. He is in fact what his faith makes him.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.3 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, the faith of all beings is in accordance with their minds. This person is made up of faith as the dominant factor. He is verily what his faith is.

records.sanskrit:
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः।
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥
records.iast:
yajante sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ
pretānbhūtagaṇāṃścānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The "soothfast" souls adore true gods; the souls
  Obeying Rajas worship Rakshasas[FN#34]
  Or Yakshas; and the men of Darkness pray
  To Pretas and to Bhutas.[FN#35]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.4 The Sattvic or the pure men worship the gods; the Rajasic or the passionate worship the Yakshas and the Rakshasas; the others (the Tamasic or the deluded people) worship the ghosts and the hosts of the nature-spirits.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.4 The Pure worship the true God; the Passionate, the powers of wealth and magic; the Ignorant, the spirits of the dead and of the lower orders of nature.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.4 Those having the sattva ality worship the gods; those having rajas, the demi-gods and ogres; and other people possessed of tamas worship ghosts and the hosts of spirits.

records.sanskrit:
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।
दम्भाहंकारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥
records.iast:
aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ
dambhāhaṃkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yea, and those
  Who  practise bitter penance, not enjoined
  By rightful rule--penance which hath its root
  In self-sufficient, proud hypocrisies--
  Those men, passion-beset, violent, wild,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.5 Those men who practise terrific austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, impelled by the force of lust and attachment.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.5 Those who practise austerities not commanded by scripture, who are slaves to hypocrisy and egotism, who are carried away by the fury of desire and passion,

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.5 Those persons who, given to ostentation and pride, and possessed of passion, attachment and strength, undertake severe austerities not sanctioned in the scriptures;

records.sanskrit:
कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः।
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥
records.iast:
karṣayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ
māṃ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Torturing--the witless ones--My elements
  Shut in fair company within their flesh,
  (Nay, Me myself, present within the flesh!)
  Know them to devils devoted, not to Heaven!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.6 Senseless, torturing all the elements in the body and Me also, Who dwell in the body, know thou these to be of demonical resolves.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.6 They are ignorant. They torment the organs of the body; and they harass Me also, Who lives within. Know that they are devoted to evil.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.6 (And who,) being non-discriminating, torture, all the organs in the body as also even Me who reside in the body,-know them as possessed of demoniacal conviction.

records.sanskrit:
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः।
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥
records.iast:
āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ
yajñastapastathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedamimaṃ śṛṇu
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
For like as foods are threefold for mankind
  In nourishing, so is there threefold way
  Of worship, abstinence, and almsgiving!
  Hear this of Me!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.7 The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.7 The food which men enjoy is also threefold, like the ways of sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Listen to the distinction.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.7 Food also, which is dear to all, is of three kinds; and so also are sacrifices, austerity and charity. Listen to this classification of them.

records.sanskrit:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
records.iast:
āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
there is a food which brings
  Force, substance, strength, and health, and joy to live,
  Being well-seasoned, cordial, comforting,
  The "Soothfast" meat.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.8 The foods which increase life, purity, strength, health, joy and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savoury and oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.8 The foods that prolong life and increase purity, vigour, health, cheerfulness and happiness are those that are delicious, soothing, substantial and agreeable. These are loved by the Pure.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.8 Foods that augment life, firmless of mind, strength, health, happiness and delight, and which are succulent, oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to one endowed with sattva.

records.sanskrit:
कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः।
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥
records.iast:
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ
āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And there be foods which bring
  Aches and unrests, and burning blood, and grief,
  Being too biting, heating, salt, and sharp,
  And therefore craved by too strong appetite.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.9 The foods that are bitter, sour, saline, excessively hot, pungent, dry and burning, are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief and disease.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.9 Those in whom Passion is dominant like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning. These produce unhappiness, repentance and disease.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.9 Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning, and which production pain, sorrow and disease, are dear to one having rajas.

records.sanskrit:
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥
records.iast:
yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat
ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And there is foul food--kept from over-night,[FN#36]
  Savourless, filthy, which the foul will eat,
  A feast of rottenness, meet for the lips
  Of such as love the "Darkness."

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.10 That which is state, tasteless, putrid, rotten, refuse and impure, is the food liked by the Tamasic.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.10 The Ignorant love food which is stale, not nourishing, putrid and corrupt, the leavings of others and unclean.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.10 Food which is not properly cooked, lacking in essence, putrid and stale, and even ort and that which is unfit for sacrifice, is dear to one possessed of tamas.

records.sanskrit:
अफलाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥
records.iast:
aphalāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate
yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Thus with rites;--
  A sacrifice not for rewardment made,
  Offered in rightful wise, when he who vows
  Sayeth, with heart devout, "This I should do!"
  Is "Soothfast" rite.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.11 That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that to do so is a duty, is Sattvic or pure.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.11 Sacrifice is Pure when it is offered by one who does not covet the fruit thereof, when it is done according to the commands of scripture, and with implicit faith that the sacrifice is a duty.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.11 That sacrifice which is in accordance with the injunctions, (and is) performed by persons who do not hanker after results, and with the mental conviction that it is surely obligatory, is done through sattva.

records.sanskrit:
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
records.iast:
abhisandhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yat
ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But sacrifice for gain,
  Offered for good repute, be sure that this,
  O Best of Bharatas! is Rajas-rite,
  With stamp of "passion."

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.12 The sacrifice which is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for ostentation, know thou that to be a Rajasic Yajna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.12 Sacrifice which is performed for the sake of its results, or for self-glorification - that, O best of Aryans, is the product of Passion.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.12 But that sacrifice which is performed having in veiw a result, as also for ostentation,-know that sacrifice to be done through rajas, O greatest among the descendants of Bharata.

records.sanskrit:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम्।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥
records.iast:
vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam
śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And a sacrifice
  Offered against the laws, with no due dole
  Of food-giving, with no accompaniment
  Of hallowed hymn, nor largesse to the priests,
  In faithless celebration, call it vile,
  The deed of "Darkness!"--lost!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.13 They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, which is devoid of Mantras, gifts and faith.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.13 Sacrifice that is contrary to scriptural command, that is unaccompanied by prayers or gifts of food or money, and is without faith - that is the product of Ignorance.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.13 They declare that sacrifice as 'done through tamas' which is contrary to injunction, in which food is not distributed, in which mantras are not used, in which offerings are not made to priests, and which is devoid of faith.

records.sanskrit:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम्।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥
records.iast:
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam
brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Worship of gods
  Meriting worship; lowly reverence
  Of Twice-borns, Teachers, Elders; Purity,
  Rectitude, and the Brahmacharya's vow,
  And not to injure any helpless thing,--
  These make a true religiousness of Act.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.14 Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers and the wise, purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-injury are called the austerities of the body.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.14 Worship of God and the Master; respect for the preacher and the philosopher; purity, rectitude, continence and harmlessness - all this is physical austerity.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.14 The worship of gods, twice-borns, venerable persons and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-injury,-are said to be bodily austerity.

records.sanskrit:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
records.iast:
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat
svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Words causing no man woe, words ever true,
  Gentle and pleasing words, and those ye say
  In murmured reading of a Sacred Writ,--
  These make the true religiousness of Speech.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.15 Speech which causes no excitement, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Vedas, are called austerity of speech.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.15 Speech that hurts no one, that is true, is pleasant to listen to and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures - this is austerity in speech.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.15 That speech which causes no pain, which is true, agreeable and beneficial; as well as the practice of study of the scriptures,-is said to be austerity of speech.

records.sanskrit:
मनः प्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥
records.iast:
manaḥ prasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ
bhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Serenity of soul, benignity,
  Sway of the silent Spirit, constant stress
  To sanctify the Nature,--these things make
  Good rite, and true religiousness of Mind.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.16 Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, purity of nature this is called mental austerity.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.16 Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control and purity - this is austerity of mind.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.16 Tranillity of mind, gentleness, reticence, withdrawal of the mind, purity of heart,-these are what is called mental austerity.

records.sanskrit:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः।
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥
records.iast:
śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastattrividhaṃ naraiḥ
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Such threefold faith, in highest piety
  Kept, with no hope of gain, by hearts devote,
  Is perfect work of Sattwan, true belief.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.17 This threefold austerity, practised by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, they call Sattvic.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.17 These threefold austerities performed with faith, and without thought of reward, may truly be accounted Pure.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.17 When that threefold austerity is undertaken with supreme faith by people who do not hanker after results and are self-controlled, they speak of it as born of sattva.

records.sanskrit:
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
records.iast:
satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat
kriyate tadiha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Religion shown in act of proud display
  To win good entertainment, worship, fame,
  Such--say I--is of Rajas, rash and vain.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.18 The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining good reception, honour and worship, and with hypocrisy, is here said to be Rajasic, unstable and transitory.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.18 Austerity coupled with hypocrisy or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity or vanity, comes from Passion, and its result is always doubtful and temporary.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.18 That austerity which is undertaken for earning a name, being honoured and worshipped, and also ostentatiously,-that is spoken of as born of rajas, belonging to this world, uncertain and transitory.

records.sanskrit:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
records.iast:
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ
parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Religion followed by a witless will
  To torture self, or come at power to hurt
  Another,--'tis of Tamas, dark and ill.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.19 That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be Tamasic.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.19 Austerity done under delusion, and accompanied with sorcery or torture to oneself or another, may be assumed to spring from Ignorance.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.19 That austerity which is undertaken with a foolish intent, by causing pain to oneself, or for the destruction of others-that is said to be born of tamas.

records.sanskrit:
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
records.iast:
dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate.anupakāriṇe
deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The gift lovingly given, when one shall say
  "Now must I gladly give!" when he who takes
  Can render nothing back; made in due place,
  Due time, and to a meet recipient,
  Is gift of Sattwan, fair and profitable.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.20 That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that gift is held to be Sattvic.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.20 The gift which is given without thought of recompense, in the belief that it ought to be made, in a fit place, at an opportune time and to a deserving person - such a gift is Pure.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.20 That gift is referred to as born of sattva which gift is given with the idea that it ought to be given, to one who will not serve in return, and at the (proper) place, (proper) time and to a (proper) person.

records.sanskrit:
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
records.iast:
yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ
dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The gift selfishly given, where to receive
  Is hoped again, or when some end is sought,
  Or where the gift is proffered with a grudge,
  This is of Rajas, stained with impulse, ill.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.21 And, that gift which is given with a view to receive something in return, or looking for a reward, or reluctantly, is held to be Rajasic.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.21 That which is given for the sake of the results it will produce, or with the hope of recompense,or grudgingly - that may truly be said to be the outcome of Passion.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.21 But the gift which is given expecting reciprocation, or again, with a desire for its result, and which is given grudgingly,- that is considered to be born of rajas.

records.sanskrit:
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते।
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
records.iast:
adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate
asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The gift churlishly flung, at evil time,
  In wrongful place, to base recipient,
  Made in disdain or harsh unkindliness,
  Is gift of Tamas, dark; it doth not bless![FN#37]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.22 The gift that is given at a wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult is declared to be Tamasic.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.22 And that which is given at an unsuitable place or time or to one who is unworthy, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of Ignorance.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.22 The gift which is made at an improper place and time, and to undeserving persons, without proper treatment and with disdain, is declared to be born of tamas.

records.sanskrit:
ॐतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥
records.iast:
OMtatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ
brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.23 "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that were created formerly, the Brahmanas, the Vedas and the sacrifices.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.23 Om Tat Sat' is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which of old the Vedic Scriptures, the ceremonials and the sacrifices were ordained.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.23 'Om-tat-sat' ['Om, That, Existence': 'Om iti brahma, Om is Brahman' (Tai. 1.8.1); 'Tattvamasi, Thou art That' (Ch. 6.8.7); and 'Sadeva somya idamagra asit, This was Existence alone in the beginning, O amiable one' (Ch. 6.2.1)-in these texts Brahman is indicated by the words Om, tat, sat.]-this is considered to be the threefold designation of Brahman. The Brahmanas and Vedas and the sacrifices were ordanined by that in the days of yore.

records.sanskrit:
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥
records.iast:
tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.24 Therefore, with the utterance of "Om" are the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as enjoined in the scriptures, always begun by the students of Brahman.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.24 Therefore all acts of sacrifice, gifts and austerities, prescribed by the scriptures, are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word Om.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.24 Therefore, acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity as prescribed through injunctions, of those who study and expound the Vedas, always commence after uttering the syllable Om.

records.sanskrit:
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥
records.iast:
tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ
dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.25 Uttering ï1Tatï1, without aiming at the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice and austerity and the various acts of gifts performed by the seekers of liberation.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.25 Those who desire deliverance begin their acts of sacrifice, austerity or gift with the word Tat' (meaning That'), without thought of reward.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.25 After (uttering) the word tat, acts of sacrifice and austerity as also the various acts of charity are performed without regard for results by persons aspiring for Liberation.

records.sanskrit:
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते।
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
records.iast:
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate
praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.26 The word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of reality and of goodness; and so also, O Arjuna, the word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of an auspicious act.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.26 Sat' means Reality or the highest Good, and also, O Arjuna, it is used to mean an action of exceptional merit.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.26 This word sat is used with regard to (something) coming into being and with regard to (someone) becoming good. So also, O son of Prtha, the word sat is used with regard to an auspicious rite.

records.sanskrit:
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥
records.iast:
yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate
karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.27 Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift, is also called 'Sat' and also action in connection with these (or for the sake of the Supreme) is called 'Sat'.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.27 Conviction in sacrifice, in austerity and in giving is also called Sat.' So too an action done only for the Lord's sake.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.27 And the steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and charity is spoken of as sat. And even the action meant for these is, verily, called as sat (good).

records.sanskrit:
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
records.iast:
aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat
asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatprepya no iha
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 17.28 Whatever is sacrificed, given or performed, and whatever austerity is practised without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is naught here or hereafter (after death).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 17.28 Whatsoever is done without faith, whether it be sacrifice, austerity or gift or anything else, as called Asat' (meaning Unreal') for it is the negation of Sat,' O Arjuna! Such an act has no significance, here or hereafter."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 17.28 O son of Prtha, whatever is offered in sacrifice and given in charity, as also whatever austerity is undertakne or whatever is done without, faith, is said to be of on avail. And it is of no conseence after death, nor here.
